Actual use requires authenticated external services, reference uploads when requested, and paid generation with documented spending confirmations.

content.user_title: Generate Game Assets with Layer MCP
content.value_statement: Creative teams need to coordinate models, reference files, and costs across asset generation tasks. This skill guides Layer MCP requests from workspace selection to completed assets and style warnings.
actual_capabilities: Guide Layer MCP generation and editing requests for images, video, 3D meshes, and audio.
Discover workspace models using task filters, required capabilities, price limits, and model requirements.
Estimate Creative Unit costs before execution and request explicit confirmation above 20 CUs or for planned sequences.
Prepare local or public reference uploads and reuse generated file identifiers in later runs.
Apply trained reference styles and report degradation warnings from estimates, execution, and polling.
Monitor runs at returned intervals and guide recovery from authentication, model, balance, rate limit, and feature errors.
limitations: Requires a configured Layer MCP connection, completed OAuth authentication, and access to the selected workspace.
Generation consumes Creative Units, and available models and features depend on workspace access.
This package contains guidance only; specialized techniques, connection setup, and workflow details refer to separate skills.
Batch generation creates variations of one prompt, and requested reference styles may degrade even when a paid run succeeds.

use_cases.title: Produce Sprite Variations
use_cases.description: Create variations of a building sprite prompt after selecting a suitable model and reviewing the estimated workspace cost.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Trained Visual Style
use_cases.description: Apply workspace reference sets across asset requests and identify any styles that fail to apply.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Creative Production
use_cases.description: Prepare reference files, estimate a sequence budget, and track image or video generation through completion.

prompt_templates.title: Discover a Suitable Model
prompt_templates.prompt: In [workspace], find a model for [asset type] and check its requirements. Report available options without starting generation.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Costed Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Create four variations of [sprite prompt] in [workspace]. Estimate cost first, apply the spending gate, and return completed asset links.

prompt_templates.title: Use References and Trained Styles
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [reference file] and [trained style] in [workspace] for [asset]. Estimate first, report style warnings, and obtain required approval before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Run Production Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan separate runs for [asset list] in [workspace]. Present total estimated cost for approval, reuse file identifiers, and monitor results and style degradation.

output_examples.input: Explain the cost decision in the documented four-sprite example.
output: The example estimates four variations at 7 CUs against a balance of 900 CUs.
This single run is below the 20 CU confirmation threshold.
Four distinct sprite prompts require separate runs and approval of the planned sequence cost.

output_examples.input: A trained style did not apply, but the generation completed. Explain the result.
output: The generation completed, but the requested trained style did not apply.
The run still consumes Creative Units.
Report the affected style and the returned warning before presenting the assets.

output_examples.input: A model identifier returns MODEL_NOT_FOUND. What should happen next?
output: Discover available models again in the selected workspace.
Check the replacement model requirements and obtain a new price estimate before execution.
Do not reuse or guess the unavailable identifier.

best_practices: Confirm the paying workspace, discover models for the task, and review their requirements before preparing a run.
Estimate every run and present planned sequence totals before obtaining required approval, even when negative balances are allowed.
Reuse generated file identifiers, follow returned polling intervals, and report reference style warnings accurately.
anti_patterns: Guessing model identifiers or filtering out suitable models with unnecessary capability settings.
Executing without an estimate or treating negative balance permission as approval to bypass spending confirmation.
Treating batch variations as distinct assets or reporting degraded reference styles as successfully applied.

faq.question: What must I connect before using this skill?
faq.answer: Connect your MCP client to the documented Layer endpoint, complete OAuth, and select an accessible workspace. Connection instructions are in a separate skill.

faq.question: Which asset types does the guidance cover?
faq.answer: It covers model selection for images, video, 3D meshes, and audio. Specialized craft guidance refers to related skills.

faq.question: When is spending confirmation required?
faq.answer: Single runs above 20 CUs require explicit approval. Planned sequences require presenting their total cost for agreement before starting.

faq.question: Can one batch create several different assets?
faq.answer: A batch creates variations of one prompt, with sizes from 1 to 16. Distinct prompts require separate runs.

faq.question: How are reference files provided?
faq.answer: Local files use signed upload URLs. Public files use the import tool, while completed assets reuse their existing file identifiers.

faq.question: Does a completed run guarantee that my trained style applied?
faq.answer: No. Check degradation warnings during estimation, execution, and polling. A successful run can still omit the requested style and consume credits.
